## KRISHIV_AUTH_IMPERSONATION_DENIED

SQLSTATE `42501`.

~~~text
The caller may not act for this user. An administrator grants acting for others with "krishiv.auth.principals.CALLER.privileges" = impersonate and lists whom in "krishiv.auth.principals.CALLER.impersonates", where CALLER is the caller's principal name; the server's audit log has the reason.
~~~

## KRISHIV_CATALOG_DELEGATION_UNAVAILABLE

SQLSTATE `42501`.

~~~text

~~~

## KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_HANDLE_LIMIT

SQLSTATE `53400`.

~~~text
Cannot create a new Arrow Flight SQL handle: <limitName> allows at most <limit>. Close prepared statements and fetch or cancel statement tickets you no longer need, or raise "<limitName>".
~~~

## KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_INVALID_PARAMETERS

SQLSTATE `07001`.

~~~text
The parameter rows bound to an Arrow Flight SQL prepared statement cannot be used: <reason>. Nothing was run.
~~~

## KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_METADATA_TIMEOUT

SQLSTATE `HY008`.

~~~text
The Arrow Flight SQL <command> listing ran longer than its limit of <limit> and was stopped. Narrow its patterns, or raise "krishiv.flightSql.metadataTimeout".
~~~

## KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_NOT_A_QUERY

SQLSTATE `55000`.

~~~text
This Arrow Flight SQL call needs a query, but the statement is not a query (its class is <statementClass>; it may have become a command through a changed ${...} variable). Nothing was run. Send it as a statement update (DoPut) or with GetFlightInfo of a new statement.
~~~

## KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_QUERY_AS_UPDATE

SQLSTATE `42000`.

~~~text
An Arrow Flight SQL update (DoPut) needs a statement that returns no rows, but this statement is a query. Nothing was run. Send it with GetFlightInfo and fetch its rows with DoGet.
~~~

## KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_RESULT_NOT_STORED

SQLSTATE `55000`.

~~~text
The statement ran; its result (<size>) was not stored: <reason>. Do not run it again to see its effect; send a query to read the state it changed.
~~~

## KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_ROW_TOO_LARGE

SQLSTATE `54000`.

~~~text
A result row of <columns> columns is larger than the <limit>-byte Arrow Flight SQL message limit and cannot be sent. Select fewer or smaller columns.
~~~

## KRISHIV_FLIGHT_SQL_SCHEMA_CHANGED

## KRISHIV_ICEBERG_COMMIT_FAILED

SQLSTATE `40001`.

~~~text
The commit of snapshot <snapshotId> (write <writeId>) to the Iceberg table <table> was not applied in any of <attempts> requests, the last answered with: <reason>. The write is not committed; <files>. Raising "commit.retry.num-retries" or "commit.retry.total-timeout-ms" on the table allows more attempts.
~~~

## KRISHIV_ICEBERG_COMMIT_STATE_UNKNOWN

SQLSTATE `40003`.

~~~text
The commit of snapshot <snapshotId> (write <writeId>) to the Iceberg table <table> may or may not have been applied: <reason>. Look for the snapshot id or the "krishiv.write-id" summary value in the table's snapshots before writing the data again.
Cannot determine whether the commit was successful or not, the underlying data files may or may not be needed. Manual intervention via the Remove Orphan Files Action can remove these files when a connection to the Catalog can be re-established if the commit was actually unsuccessful.
Please check to see whether or not your commit was successful before retrying this commit. Retrying an already successful operation will result in duplicate records or unintentional modifications.
At this time no files will be deleted including possibly unused manifest lists.
~~~

## KRISHIV_PYTHON_ARTIFACT_REFUSED

SQLSTATE `22023`.

~~~text
The Python artifact <name> cannot be used by UDF workers: <reason>. Add a smaller or a well-formed artifact (zip, jar, tar, tar.gz or tgz archives), or raise the server's artifact limit.
~~~

## KRISHIV_PYTHON_DATA_SOURCE_LIMIT

SQLSTATE `53400`.

~~~text
The Python data source <source> returned <bytes> bytes, over the <limit> byte limit of this embedded read path, which holds a source's rows in memory when a scan runs. Read less of it per query (narrow the source's options or split it into smaller sources).
~~~

## KRISHIV_PYTHON_UDF_EVAL_TYPE_MISMATCH

SQLSTATE `39000`.

~~~text
The Python UDF <name>@<version> is registered with eval type <registered> but the plan calls it as <called> (eval type <evalType>): register the function on the executing session as the kind of call the query makes.
~~~

## KRISHIV_PYTHON_UDF_RESULT_MISMATCH

SQLSTATE `39000`.

~~~text
The Python UDF <name> returned a result that does not match what it declares: <reason>. Make the function return the declared columns, in their declared types, and for a grouped aggregate one value per group.
~~~

## KRISHIV_PYTHON_WORKER_EXITED

SQLSTATE `38000`.

~~~text
Python worker exited unexpectedly (crashed): <reason>. The next query starts a new worker. If a UDF ran out of memory, raise "krishiv.python.worker.memoryLimit".
~~~

## KRISHIV_PYTHON_WORKER_LIMIT

SQLSTATE `54000`.

~~~text
<operation> needs <needed> Python UDF workers at once, and at most <available> can serve it: "<setting>" is <value>, and one of those workers is kept for scalar Python UDFs when there are 2 or more. Raise "<setting>", or call fewer Python UDFs in one operator.
~~~

~~~

## KRISHIV_REGEXP_BACKTRACK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED

SQLSTATE `54000`.

~~~text
Matching the pattern <pattern> in <functionName> exceeded the backtracking limit of <limit> steps on one input, so the query was stopped. Simplify the pattern (nested or overlapping quantifiers such as `(a+)+` backtrack exponentially). Spark on the JVM has no such limit and would keep running.
~~~
